title: Shanghai and the Orient trip with Jack Carter; Moscow
summary: Howard leaves King Oliver's Plantation to join Jack Carter's group for a long hotel and steamship tour of Asia, and mentions playing Moscow twice.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: 1923. Oh, did you go to Europe in 23? Uh-huh. Come right back off the road and working with Carol Dixon and Jack Carter, says, boy, let's go to China. I said, man, no, I've just come back off of that thing. I don't want to move, you know. So he left. I was working at the Plantation with King Oliver. Something happened that got me disgusted and Jack's wife come in there and she says, anything you want me to tell Jack, I'm going to Shanghai. We're leaving in the morning, you know. I said, well, ask him if that offer is still good. He says, are you serious? I said, sure, I'm serious. He said, well, I'm going out and sending him a cable now. And sure enough, she got a cable from that answer before we close that morning. Right in the cafe. Bring all new music. No kidding. I'll never forget that. Oh, I was so happy. That was a wonderful trip to TKK, Toria Kisenkisen, Oriental Steamship Hotel System. Took me all the way around. I wish they'd had something like that now. Where did you play? Played all countries. Oriental Steamship Hotel System, like in Shanghai, was our headquarters for a while. The Dollar Line would come in on Monday, stay two days, leave around noon on Wednesday. The Canadian Pacific would come in that Wednesday morning, stay the Friday. The United States Lines would come in, President Harding, Monroe, you know, those different ones. And we were off Sunday. That's the same routine. We didn't play on the boats, but those are the boats. See, I left here and went on the Taiyo Maru. That's the Japanese boat. Went to Shanghai direct. But, see, I've been very fortunate. I've been to Moscow twice. Wilhelmina Hotel, went back and played at the National Hotel. When was that?

New York singing syncopated Jack Carter, Will Hageman. You know Bill Hageman, don't you? Why name? Bill Hageman and Jack Carter, Barry Jansett, there's only two of us living. Now, I was the piano player myself. Jack Carter, you know, died. What did he play? Drums. Drums. Sand, dance. You know what was amusing about that job? We had two Filipinas with us. There was six of us.
This was the job in Shanghai?

Well, it went all over. Going all over. Like, I got a specialty this week. After this week, there's eight of us, see. I got eight more weeks to get another one in. Each week somebody did something, you know. And, man, they had a Russian ballet with us. We didn't play any of the show, we just did our specialty in the show. Now, listen, Nazmi. If you're going to do that, that my conversation is often dull, you just getting ready to go to sleep. Not at all. Not at all.
You should see him. You know what I'm not... Set the camera in that direction.
Huh? You're jumping from one thing to another and I can't follow you.
